1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, according to the promise of life that's in Christ Jesus,
1.2: To Timothy, my beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
1.3: I thank God, whom I serve with a pure conscience, just like my forefathers did, and I keep you in my prayers day and night,
1.4: I really wanna see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy,
1.5: When I think about the real faith that's in you, the same faith that was first in your grandma Lois and your mama Eunice, and I'm sure it's in you too.
1.6: So I'm reminding you to stir up the gift of God that's inside you, the one I gave you through the laying on of my hands.
1.7: God didn't give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.
1.8: So don't be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner, but share in the suffering for the gospel with me, according to God's power.
1.9: God saved us and called us with a holy calling, not because of anything we did, but because of His own purpose and grace, which He gave us in Christ Jesus before time even began,
1.10: But now it's been revealed through the appearance of our Savior Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
1.11: That's the gospel I was called to preach, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
1.12: And because of this, I'm suffering, but I ain't ashamed, 'cause I know who I've believed in, and I'm convinced He can keep everything I've committed to Him until that Day.
1.13: Hold on to the sound words you've heard from me, in faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
1.14: The good thing that was committed to you, keep it safe by the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
1.15: You know that everyone in Asia has turned away from me, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.
1.16: But may the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he refreshed me, and wasn't ashamed of my chains.
1.17: When he came to Rome, he searched for me hard, and found me.
1.18: I pray the Lord shows him mercy on that Day—and you know how much he helped me out in Ephesus.

2.1: So, my son, be strong in the grace that's in Christ Jesus.
2.2: And the stuff you heard from me, with all the witnesses around, pass that on to faithful men who will be able to teach others too.
2.3: You gotta endure hardship like a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
2.4: When you're in a fight, don't get caught up in the world's drama. Stay focused so you can please the one who enlisted you as a soldier.
2.5: And if anyone's in a competition, they don't win unless they follow the rules.
2.6: The hard-working farmer gets the first share of the crop.
2.7: Think about what I'm saying, and I pray the Lord gives you understanding in everything.
2.8: Don't forget—Jesus Christ, from the line of David, was raised from the dead according to the gospel I'm preaching,
2.9: For which I'm suffering trouble like a criminal, even to the point of being in chains, but the word of God ain't chained.
2.10: So, I endure all this for the elect, so they can get the salvation that's in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
2.11: Here's a real saying: If we died with Him, We gon' live with Him.
2.12: If we endure, We gon' reign with Him. But if we deny Him, He gon' deny us.
2.13: If we faithless, He stays faithful; He can't deny Himself.
2.14: Remind them of these things, charge them before the Lord, not to be out here arguing over words that don't do anything but mess up the hearers.
2.15: Do your work so you can present yourself approved to God, a worker who ain't ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.
2.16: But stay away from pointless chatter, 'cause it only leads to more ungodliness.
2.17: And that kind of mess spreads like cancer. Hymenaeus and Philetus are examples of this,
2.18: They've gotten off track with the truth, saying the resurrection has already happened, and they've messed up some folks' faith.
2.19: But the solid foundation of God stands firm with this seal: "The Lord knows who belong to Him," and, "Let everyone who claims the name of Christ turn from sin."
2.20: In a big house, there's all kinds of vessels—gold and silver, but also wood and clay, some for honor and some for dishonor.
2.21: If anyone cleanses themselves from dishonorable stuff, they'll be a vessel for honor, set apart, useful to the Master, ready for every good work.
2.22: So, run from youthful desires, but pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, with those who call on the Lord with a pure heart.
2.23: Avoid all that foolish and ignorant arguing—it just causes drama.
2.24: A servant of the Lord shouldn't be out here fighting but should be gentle to everyone, able to teach, patient,
2.25: In humility, correcting those who are against the truth, hoping God will grant them repentance, so they can come to their senses and escape the devil's trap.
2.26: The devil's been using them for his own will, but God wants to set them free.

3.1: Yo, know this: In the last days, hard times are coming,
3.2: People gon' be loving themselves, loving money, boasting, proud, talking down on others, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
3.3: Unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, no self-control, brutal, haters of good,
3.4: Traitors, headstrong, cocky, lovers of pleasure instead of lovers of God,
3.5: They'll have a form of godliness, but they'll deny the real power of it. Avoid these people!
3.6: These are the ones who sneak into households and take advantage of weak women, weighed down by their sins, led away by all kinds of lust,
3.7: Always learning, but never able to really know the truth.
3.8: Just like Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, these folks resist the truth too—corrupt minds, disqualified when it comes to the faith,
3.9: But they won't get far, 'cause their foolishness will be exposed to everyone, just like the other false teachers.
3.10: But you've been following my teachings, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my patience, love, and perseverance,
3.11: You saw all the persecution and suffering I went through at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra—the troubles I faced, and out of all of it, the Lord delivered me.
3.12: Yes, everyone who wants to live godly in Christ Jesus is gon' face persecution.
3.13: But evil men and fake ones? They gon' keep getting worse—deceiving and being deceived.
3.14: But you gotta keep doing what you've learned and are sure about, knowing who you got it from.
3.15: You've known the Holy Scriptures since you was a kid, and those scriptures make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
3.16: All Scripture is inspired by God, and it's good for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness,
3.17: So that the man of God can be complete, ready for every good work.

4.1: I'm charging you before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who gon' judge the living and the dead when He shows up and His kingdom comes:
4.2: Preach the word! Be ready to speak it whether it's the right season or not. Convince, rebuke, encourage—do it all with patience and teachin'.
4.3: The time's comin' when people ain't gon' wanna hear the real gospel. They gon' want things that fit their own desires, and they gon' get people who just scratch their itching ears.
4.4: They'll turn away from the truth and start listenin' to made-up stories.
4.5: But you? Stay watchful in everything, endure the hard times, do the work of an evangelist, and finish your ministry. Keep pushing, no matter what.
4.6: Look, I'm already bein' poured out like a drink offering, and my time to dip outta here is near.
4.7: I fought the good fight, I finished the race, and I kept the faith.
4.8: Now, there's a crown of righteousness waiting for me, and the Lord, the righteous Judge, gon' give it to me on that day. Not just to me, though, but to everyone who loves His appearing.
4.10: 'Cause Demas dipped on me, loved the world more than the mission, and he went to Thessalonica. Crescens went to Galatia, Titus went to Dalmatia.
4.11: Only Luke is still here with me. Bring Mark with you—he's useful for ministry.
4.13: Bring the cloak I left with Carpus in Troas when you come—and the books, especially the parchments.
4.14: Watch out for Alexander the coppersmith—he caused me a lot of harm. May the Lord pay him back for what he did.
4.15: And you, beware of him, 'cause he fought against our message hard.
4.16: When I went to defend myself the first time, nobody stood with me—they all bounced. Don't hold it against them, though.
4.17: But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so the message could be fully preached through me, and all the Gentiles could hear it. I was delivered from the lion's mouth.
4.18: The Lord will keep delivering me from evil and preserve me for His heavenly kingdom. To Him be all the glory forever and ever. Amen!
4.19: Say what's up to Prisca and Aquila, and the house of Onesiphorus.
4.20: Erastus stayed in Corinth, but Trophimus, I left in Miletus sick.
4.21: Do everything you can to get here before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the believers send their greetings.
4.22: May the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, and may grace be with you all. Amen.
